whyEn: Exam weight 2/3, but the exam-relevant content splits sharply by licence level. On the EMR written exam this chapter is almost a non-event: COPR's 2026 exam-content rules exclude ALL named medications and ALL drug classifications from that paper. On the PCP written exam it becomes classification-only — every drug question points at one of exactly 12 categories ('a vasodilator', never 'nitroglycerin') — so the real payoff of this chapter is learning to sort BC's actual medications into those 12 drawers, plus mastering the pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics vocabulary (half-life, receptor types, routes of administration and their onset times, dose-calculation formulas) that underlies every other clinical chapter you will read. BC's EMALB practical stations and licensing exam then flip back to real drug names and real BC doses, so the 18 monographs in drugs.json still have to be learned cold — this chapter is the bridge between the two rule-sets.
whyZh: 考试权重 2/3，但可考内容按执照等级完全分裂。EMR 笔试里这一章几乎不直接出题——COPR 2026 年的考纲明确把所有具名药物和所有药物分类都排除在 EMR 笔试之外。到了 PCP 笔试就变成纯分类题：每一道药物题只会点出 12 个分类里的一个（比如「一种血管扩张药」，绝不会写「硝酸甘油」）——所以这一章真正的价值，是学会把 BC 实际用的药一个个分进这 12 个抽屉，同时吃透支撑其他所有临床章节的药代动力学/药效动力学词汇（半衰期、受体类型、给药途径与起效时间、剂量计算公式）。BC EMALB 的实操站和执照考又会切回具名药和 BC 真实剂量，所以 drugs.json 里的 18 份药物专论还是必须背熟——这一章就是连接两层规则的桥梁。

sections.titleEn: The Six Rights and Why Medication Errors Matter
sections.titleZh: 六项正确与用药错误的代价

points.en: Pharmacology is the study of how medications act on the body; medication errors are the single leading category of patient-safety error in all of health care, which is why every administration is checked against the Six Rights.
points.zh: 药理学研究药物如何作用于人体；用药错误是整个医疗体系中头号的病人安全错误类型——这正是每一次给药都要用「六项正确」核对的原因。

points.en: The Six Rights: Right Patient, Right Medication, Right Dose, Right Route, Right Time, Right Documentation/PCR reporting.
points.zh: 六项正确：正确病人、正确药物、正确剂量、正确途径、正确时间、正确记录/病历报告（PCR）。

points.en: Right Patient: verify identity before giving anything — especially when the patient is unconscious or cannot communicate — and always screen for allergies pulled from the SAMPLE history.
points.zh: 正确病人：给药前一定要核实身份——尤其是病人无意识或无法交流时——并从 SAMPLE 病史里筛查过敏史。

points.en: Right Medication: giving the wrong drug is the single most common medication error; guard against it by echoing back the order out loud and matching the packaging to what was ordered before administering.
points.zh: 正确药物：给错药是最常见的单一用药错误；预防办法是大声复述医嘱（echo back）并在给药前核对包装与医嘱是否一致。

points.en: Right Dose: prehospital dosing is patient-specific (weight, age, condition) and rarely matches the concentration supplied in the ampoule, so you calculate the actual dose yourself and, whenever possible, have a partner double-check the math.
points.zh: 正确剂量：院前剂量要按病人个体情况（体重、年龄、病情）计算，很少正好等于安瓿里现成的浓度，所以要自己算出实际剂量，条件允许时让搭档复核一遍算式。

points.en: Right Route and Right Time: the same drug can behave very differently by route (e.g. an IV bolus versus an IV drip of the same medication are different exposures), and every drug has a recommended dosing interval to keep it at a therapeutic level without stacking doses.
points.zh: 正确途径与正确时间：同一种药换个给药途径效果可能完全不同（例如同一药物的 IV 推注和 IV 持续滴注就是不同的暴露量），而每种药都有推荐给药间隔，用来维持治疗浓度、避免叠加过量。

sections.titleEn: The Two-Layer Exam Rule: COPR Classifications vs. Named Drugs
sections.titleZh: 两层考试规则：COPR 分类 vs 具名药物

points.en: Per COPR's official medication list (v1.2, Feb 2026), the EMR written exam does not test any named medication or any drug classification at all — pharmacology is essentially off that paper.
points.zh: 根据 COPR 官方药物清单（v1.2，2026 年 2 月版），EMR 笔试完全不考任何具名药物、也不考任何药物分类——药理学基本不在这张卷子上。

points.en: The PCP written exam tests classifications only, never named drugs — a question will say 'administer a sympathomimetic bronchodilator,' never 'administer salbutamol.' There are exactly 12 testable classifications on the PCP paper.
points.zh: PCP 笔试只考分类，绝不考具名药——题目会说「给予一种拟交感支气管扩张药」，绝不会写「给予沙丁胺醇」。PCP 卷子上可考的分类正好是 12 个。

points.en: The 12 PCP classifications: Antiemetic, Antihistamine, Anticholinergic bronchodilator, Antihypoglycemic hormone, Carbohydrate, Nonnarcotic analgesic, NSAID, Opioid antagonist, Platelet inhibitor, Sympathomimetic, Sympathomimetic bronchodilator, Vasodilator.
points.zh: 12 个 PCP 分类：止吐药、抗组胺药、抗胆碱能支气管扩张药、抗低血糖激素、碳水化合物、非麻醉性镇痛药、NSAID（非甾体抗炎药）、阿片拮抗剂、血小板抑制剂、拟交感药、拟交感支气管扩张药、血管扩张药。

points.en: This classification-only rule applies strictly to the written exam question stems. It does not mean you can skip learning real drugs — you still need to know which BC medication fills each classification, because the practical station and the licensing exam use real names.
points.zh: 「只考分类」这条规则只管笔试题干本身怎么问。它不代表你可以不学具名药——你仍然要知道每个分类具体对应 BC 用的哪一款药，因为实操站和执照考用的是真实药名。

points.en: BC's EMALB practical stations and the licensing exam still use real drug names and real BC-specific doses — the 18-drug monograph set (dose, route, onset, contraindications) is examinable there even though the PCP written paper never names a single drug.
points.zh: BC EMALB 的实操站和执照考仍然用真实药名和 BC 特定剂量——18 份药物专论（剂量、途径、起效时间、禁忌证）在那两关是要考的，即使 PCP 笔试从头到尾不会点出任何一个具名药。

sections.titleEn: Medication Names, Sources, and Where to Look Things Up
sections.titleZh: 药物命名、来源与查询渠道

points.en: Health Canada's Health Products and Food Branch (HPFB), under the Food and Drugs Act, is the agency that approves a substance as a legal medication in Canada.
points.zh: 加拿大卫生部下属的健康产品与食品分支（HPFB），依据《食品药品法》，是核准某种物质成为合法药物的机构。

points.en: Prescription-only medicines (POM) require a prescriber's order; over-the-counter (OTC) drugs do not. A POM can be reclassified OTC once it is judged safe enough that most people will not harm themselves following the label instructions.
points.zh: 处方药（POM）需要有处方权的医生开具医嘱；非处方药（OTC）不需要。一款处方药一旦被认定「按说明书使用大多数人不会自我伤害」，就可以改成 OTC。

points.en: Every medication carries three names: a chemical name (its molecular composition), a generic/nonproprietary name (shorter, standardized worldwide since the 1950s WHO program, finalized in Canada by Health Canada), and a trade/brand name owned by one manufacturer. Example: amiodarone (generic) is sold as Cordarone (trade).
points.zh: 每种药物都有三个名字：化学名（描述分子结构）、通用名（更短、自 1950 年代 WHO 项目起全球标准化，最终由加拿大卫生部核定）、以及某一家厂商专属的商品名。例：胺碘酮（amiodarone，通用名）的商品名是 Cordarone。

points.en: Medications come from four sources: plant (e.g. digitalis from foxglove leaves), animal (e.g. insulin from pig pancreas, Armour thyroid from desiccated pig thyroid), mineral (calcium, iron, magnesium), and laboratory-synthesized compounds (vitamins, steroids, many narcotics).
points.zh: 药物来自四大来源：植物（如毛地黄从洋地黄叶提取）、动物（如胰岛素来自猪胰腺、Armour 甲状腺素来自猪甲状腺干燥物）、矿物（钙、铁、镁）以及实验室合成（维生素、类固醇、许多麻醉药）。

points.en: Reliable drug-information sources include Health Canada's Therapeutic Products Directorate Drug Product Database (checks Canadian approval status), the Compendium of Pharmaceuticals and Specialties (CPS), hospital formularies, and manufacturer drug inserts (product monographs) — note that US references such as Epocrates, Lexi-Comp, and Micromedex may not match Canadian drug names or approvals.
points.zh: 可靠的药物信息来源包括加拿大卫生部治疗产品处的药品数据库（可查加拿大核准状态）、《加拿大药品与专科汇编》（CPS）、医院处方集，以及厂商药品说明书（产品专论）——要注意 Epocrates、Lexi-Comp、Micromedex 这类美国资源，药名或核准状态可能和加拿大对不上。

sections.titleEn: Canadian Drug Law and the Approval Pipeline
sections.titleZh: 加拿大药事法规与核准流程

points.en: The Food and Drugs Act (first passed 1920, last major revision 1985) governs the sale, advertising, and labelling of all food, drugs, natural health products, and medical devices in Canada.
points.zh: 《食品药品法》（1920 年首次通过，1985 年最近一次大修）管辖加拿大所有食品、药品、天然健康产品和医疗器械的销售、广告与标签。

points.en: The Controlled Drugs and Substances Act (1996) replaced the 1961 Narcotic Control Act and organizes controlled substances into schedules: Schedule I (narcotics — opium, heroin, morphine, cocaine), II (cannabis/cannabis resin), III (stimulants like amphetamines, hallucinogens like LSD), IV (anabolic steroids, barbiturates, benzodiazepines — no simple-possession offence, unlike I-III), VI (precursor chemicals for designer drugs), and IX (pill-press/encapsulating devices); Schedules V, VII, and VIII have been repealed.
points.zh: 《管制药物和物质法》（1996 年）取代了 1961 年的《麻醉品管制法》，把管制物质分成若干附表：附表 I（麻醉品——鸦片、海洛因、吗啡、可卡因）、II（大麻/大麻树脂）、III（兴奋剂如安非他明、致幻剂如 LSD）、IV（合成代谢类固醇、巴比妥类、苯二氮䓬类——不同于 I-III，单纯持有不构成犯罪）、VI（合成新型毒品用的前体化学品）、IX（压片/胶囊填充设备）；附表 V、VII、VIII 已被废止。

points.en: Manufactured drug content must fall within 95%-105% of the labelled dose — a tablet labelled '300 mg amiodarone' must actually contain between 285 mg and 315 mg; manufacturers verify this with an assay (analyzing the drug itself) or a bioassay (measuring its effect on a living system).
points.zh: 药物实际含量必须落在标示剂量的 95%-105% 以内——标注「300 mg 胺碘酮」的药片实际含量必须在 285-315 mg 之间；厂商用化验（assay，直接分析药物本身）或生物检定（bioassay，测量对活体系统的效应）来验证。

points.en: New drugs take an average of about 9 years from development to approval and must complete testing in at least two animal species before entering human trials, which run in four phases: Phase I (healthy volunteers, establishes safe dosing), Phase II (50-300 patients, double-blind vs. placebo, tests efficacy), Phase III (several thousand patients over several years, confirms efficacy and side-effect profile), Phase IV (after the New Drug Submission is approved, compares the drug to existing options and tracks long-term cost-effectiveness).
points.zh: 新药从研发到核准平均约需 9 年，进入人体试验前必须先完成至少两种动物物种的测试；人体试验分四期：I 期（健康志愿者，确定安全剂量）、II 期（50-300 名患者，双盲对照安慰剂，检验疗效）、III 期（数千名患者、持续数年，确认疗效和不良反应谱）、IV 期（新药申请获批后，与现有药物比较并追踪长期成本效益）。

points.en: Once approved, a drug receives a Notice of Compliance plus a unique Drug Identification Number (natural health products instead get a Natural Product Number); the Special Access Program lets practitioners obtain drugs not yet marketed in Canada for patients whose conventional therapy has failed.
points.zh: 药物核准后会获得一份「符合通知」外加唯一的药物识别号（天然健康产品则改发天然产品号）；特别使用计划（SAP）允许医生为常规治疗无效的病人申请加拿大尚未上市的药物。

sections.titleZh: 特殊人群用药：孕妇、儿童、老年人

points.en: Any drug given in pregnancy poses a double risk — altering the mother's own anatomy/physiology and potentially harming the fetus directly; Canadian providers use the same maternal/fetal risk-rating scale as the US FDA, and the MOTHERISK program at Toronto's Hospital for Sick Children maintains the world's largest public database of pregnancy drug-safety data.
points.zh: 孕期用药有双重风险——既会改变母体自身的解剖/生理，又可能直接伤害胎儿；加拿大和美国 FDA 用同一套母体/胎儿风险分级标准，多伦多病童医院的 MOTHERISK 项目维护着全球最大的公开孕期用药安全数据库。

points.en: Worked example — amiodarone in pregnancy: it is 38% iodine by weight, which can cause fetal hypothyroidism if given in the second trimester; its elimination half-life is 58 days, so breastfeeding is contraindicated after use because clinically significant amounts persist in breast milk for a very long time.
points.zh: 举例——胺碘酮在孕期：按重量算 38% 是碘，孕中期使用可能引发胎儿甲状腺功能低下；它的消除半衰期长达 58 天，所以用药后禁止哺乳，因为乳汁中会持续残留有临床意义的药量很长时间。

points.en: Infants do not reach adult-level hepatic function until roughly 6 months of age, so their metabolic capacity is sharply reduced; an immature GI tract also slows oral absorption and delays elimination, making the same oral dose more potent in an infant than in an adult. Paradoxically, children can metabolize some drugs faster than adults and may need relatively higher or more frequent dosing of those specific medications.
points.zh: 婴儿大约要到 6 个月大才达到成人水平的肝功能，代谢能力因此大幅下降；肠胃道尚未发育成熟也会拖慢口服吸收、延迟排泄，让同一口服剂量在婴儿身上比在成人身上作用更强。矛盾的是，对某些特定药物，儿童的代谢反而比成人更快，需要相对更高或更频繁的剂量。

points.en: Geriatric patients show the mirror-image pattern from a different cause: hepatic, GI, and renal function all decline with age, delaying absorption, metabolism, and elimination alike; on top of that, polypharmacy raises the risk of drug interactions, and altered mental status raises the risk of unintentional overdose or missed doses.
points.zh: 老年病人呈现方向相反但同样麻烦的模式：肝、胃肠、肾功能都随年龄下降，同时拖慢吸收、代谢和排泄；再加上多重用药本身就增加相互作用风险，认知状态的改变又增加了意外过量或漏服的风险。

sections.titleEn: Scope, Legal Responsibility, and Getting a Medication History
sections.titleZh: 执业范围、法律责任与用药史采集

points.en: Administering medications is one of the biggest differences between a paramedic's scope and a first responder's — the wrong drug or the wrong dose of the right drug can kill a patient as surely as a weapon, so indications, contraindications, side effects, and dangers must be second nature before you give anything.
points.zh: 给药是急救员执业范围和第一响应者最大的区别之一——用错药或者对药用错剂量，杀伤力不亚于一件武器，所以适应证、禁忌证、副作用和危险性必须在给药前就烂熟于心。

points.en: Legal responsibility for a medication follows whoever administers it, even if a colleague drew it up and handed you the syringe — you must independently understand what you are giving and why before you give it.
points.zh: 用药的法律责任归给药的人承担，即使药是搭档抽好、递给你打的——给之前你必须自己独立弄清楚给的是什么、为什么给。

points.en: 'Do not trust your memory in an emergency' — always confirm precautions and contraindications against a reference rather than recalling from memory under stress; error-prone abbreviations (per the Institute for Safe Medication Practices) are a known source of miscommunication and should be avoided in verbal and written orders.
points.zh: 「紧急情况下不要相信自己的记忆」——永远对照参考资料核实注意事项和禁忌证，而不是在压力下凭记忆回想；安全用药规范协会（ISMP）列出的易错缩写是已知的沟通错误来源，口头和书面医嘱都应避免使用。

points.en: Get a thorough medication history beyond just prescriptions: ask about OTC drugs, recreational drugs, vitamins, herbal remedies, and alternative medicines, since any of these can interact with what you plan to give — or may even be the cause of the patient's current presentation. The patient retains the right to refuse treatment after being fully informed of risks and side effects.
points.zh: 用药史采集不能只问处方药：还要问 OTC 药、娱乐性药物、维生素、草药和替代疗法，因为这些都可能和你打算给的药相互作用——甚至可能就是病人当前症状的病因。病人在被充分告知风险和副作用后，仍保留拒绝治疗的权利。

sections.titleZh: 药物的一般特性与剂型

points.en: Medications usually adjust functions the body already has rather than granting it new ones; the most common mechanism in prehospital care is binding to a receptor site, where affinity (bond strength) decides which of several competing drugs or mediators wins that receptor, and the size of the response scales with how many receptor sites are occupied.
points.zh: 药物通常是调节身体已有的功能，而不是凭空赋予新功能；院前最常见的作用机制是结合受体位点，亲和力（结合强度）决定几种互相竞争的药物或介质中谁能占到这个受体，反应的大小则和被占据的受体数量成正比。

points.en: Liquid forms: solution (fully dissolved, most drugs paramedics use are this form), suspension (must be shaken before use — e.g. reconstituted amoxicillin), tincture/elixir (alcohol-based), and emulsion (oil droplets in water, e.g. some diazepam preparations).
points.zh: 液体剂型：溶液（完全溶解，急救员用的大多数药都是这种）、混悬液（用前必须摇匀——如需要加水冲配的阿莫西林）、酊剂/酏剂（含酒精）、乳剂（油滴分散在水中，如部分安定制剂）。

points.en: Solid forms: the tablet is the most-used solid dosage form (e.g. nitroglycerin tablets), with enteric-coated, rapid-dissolve, chewable, and effervescent variants; a suppository can act locally (glycerin, to promote defecation) or systemically (rectal diazepam for status epilepticus in children); a transdermal patch delivers a slow, sustained dose through the skin (e.g. nitroglycerin patch).
points.zh: 固体剂型：药片是最常用的固体剂型（如硝酸甘油片），衍生出肠溶、速溶、可嚼、泡腾等变体；栓剂可以是局部作用（甘油栓促排便）也可以是全身作用（儿童癫痫持续状态用的直肠地西泮栓）；透皮贴剂通过皮肤缓慢持续给药（如硝酸甘油贴）。

points.en: Gaseous/vapour forms are mainly anesthetics vapourized by a machine and inhaled; methoxyflurane (Penthrox) is a Health Canada-approved inhaled anesthetic for prehospital mild-to-moderate pain, self-administered, limited to a maximum of two doses, and not used in patients under 18 years old or who are pregnant.
points.zh: 气体/蒸气剂型主要是靠机器气化后吸入的麻醉药；甲氧氟烷（Penthrox）是加拿大卫生部核准用于院前轻中度疼痛的吸入麻醉药，病人自行吸入，最多用两剂，18 岁以下和孕妇不得使用。

sections.titleZh: 各给药途径的吸收速率：Table 7-4

points.en: Local effects come from a drug applied directly to a tissue (e.g. a lotion on the skin); systemic effects follow absorption into the bloodstream and typically involve more than one organ. The same drug's actual effect always depends on the patient, the dose, the route, and the patient's metabolic rate — it is never a fixed property of the drug alone.
points.zh: 局部效应来自药物直接作用于某个组织（比如涂在皮肤上的乳膏）；全身效应则要先被吸收进血液，通常会牵涉不止一个器官。同一种药的实际效果永远取决于病人本身、剂量、给药途径和代谢速率——绝不是药物单方面固定不变的属性。

points.en: Fastest to slowest onset by route (healthy patient, normal perfusion): intracardiac and IV/IO among the fastest, then sublingual/inhaled/tracheal, then rectal, then SC, then IM, then oral, with topical absorption through intact skin the slowest of all (hours to days).
points.zh: 起效速度由快到慢（健康人、灌注正常时）：心内注射和 IV/IO 最快，接着是舌下/吸入/气管给药，再来是直肠、皮下、肌肉，口服更慢，完整皮肤的局部给药全场最慢（数小时到数天）。

points.en: Table 7-4 onset times by route: topical hours-days; oral 30-90 min; rectal 5-30 min (unpredictable); SC injection 15-30 min; IM injection 10-20 min; sublingual tablet 3-5 min; sublingual spray 3 min; inhalation 3 min; tracheal unknown/unpredictable; IO 60 seconds (best alternate route when no IV access); IV 30-60 seconds; intracardiac 15 seconds (no longer recommended in cardiac arrest).
points.zh: Table 7-4 各途径起效时间：局部（皮肤）数小时至数天；口服 30-90 分钟；直肠 5-30 分钟（不可预测）；皮下注射 15-30 分钟；肌肉注射 10-20 分钟；舌下含片 3-5 分钟；舌下喷雾 3 分钟；吸入 3 分钟；气管给药未知/不可预测；骨髓腔（IO）60 秒（无 IV 通路时的最佳替代途径）；静脉（IV）30-60 秒；心内注射 15 秒（心脏骤停时已不再推荐）。

sections.titleEn: Routes of Administration: Percutaneous, Enteral, Parenteral
sections.titleZh: 给药途径：经皮、肠道与肠外

points.en: Three route categories by absorption path: percutaneous (through skin or mucous membrane), enteral (somewhere along the GI tract, most often oral), and parenteral (everything else — by definition, not skin, mucous membrane, or GI tract, typically via needle/syringe).
points.zh: 按吸收路径分三大类：经皮（经皮肤或黏膜）、肠道（经消化道，最常见是口服）、肠外（其余所有途径——按定义就是不经皮肤、黏膜或消化道，通常用针头/注射器）。

points.en: Transdermal absorption is slow and sustained through intact skin (e.g. nitroglycerin cream/patch, estrogen patch); its rate is steady but is slowed by thick skin, scar tissue, or reduced peripheral circulation (hypothermia, hypotension), and sped up by fever.
points.zh: 透皮吸收经完整皮肤，缓慢而持续（如硝酸甘油乳膏/贴剂、雌激素贴）；速率虽然稳定，但皮肤增厚、瘢痕组织或外周循环下降（低体温、低血压）会拖慢它，发热则会加快它。

points.en: Mucosal routes absorb at a moderate-to-rapid rate: sublingual (e.g. nitroglycerin, effect within minutes), buccal (e.g. glucose gel for a conscious hypoglycemic patient), and intranasal — naloxone given IN is absorbed quickly through the rich nasopharyngeal vasculature, which is why public take-home naloxone kits default to the intranasal route.
points.zh: 黏膜给药吸收速度中等偏快：舌下（如硝酸甘油，数分钟内起效）、颊黏膜（如给清醒的低血糖病人用葡萄糖凝胶）、鼻内——鼻内给纳洛酮能经鼻咽部丰富的血管迅速吸收，这也是公众自带纳洛酮急救包默认走鼻内途径的原因。

points.en: Pulmonary route: nebulized mist inhaled into the bronchioles/alveoli, or liquid medication instilled directly down a tracheal tube. Only four drugs are considered suitable for the tracheal route — mnemonic ALIEN: Atropine, Lidocaine, Epinephrine, Naloxone — and the tracheal dose must be doubled versus the IV dose for an equivalent effect; the tracheal route is no longer recommended in cardiac arrest because absorption there is unreliable, and IV/IO are preferred instead.
points.zh: 肺部途径：雾化吸入到细支气管/肺泡，或把液体药物直接灌进气管导管。适合气管给药的药物按记忆法 ALIEN 只有四个：阿托品（Atropine）、利多卡因（Lidocaine）、肾上腺素（Epinephrine）、纳洛酮（Naloxone）——而且气管给药剂量要翻倍于 IV 剂量才能达到同等效果；心脏骤停时已不再推荐气管途径，因为吸收不可靠，改用 IV/IO。

points.en: Enteral (oral) is painless, convenient, and cheap but slow and unpredictable — usually 30-90 minutes — so it is rarely used in true emergencies; the classic exception is chewed ASA for suspected acute coronary syndrome, which still requires adequate consciousness to avoid aspiration. Rectal administration bypasses the liver's first-pass effect and is useful when IV access is impractical, but the rectum's rich vascularity makes absorption fast yet unpredictable.
points.zh: 肠道（口服）无痛、方便、便宜，但慢而不可预测——通常要 30-90 分钟——所以真正的急症很少用；经典例外是疑似急性冠脉综合征时嚼服阿司匹林，但仍要求病人意识清醒以免误吸。直肠给药能绕开肝脏的首过效应，在 IV 通路不方便建立时很有用，但直肠血管丰富，吸收快却不可预测。

points.en: IV is the fastest and most dangerous route: the entire dose enters at once, so equalization of blood concentration takes about 30-60 seconds normally, but during CPR in cardiac arrest a drug takes 3-4 times longer to reach its target because cardiac output is only about one-third of normal — wait at least 1-2 minutes to judge effect, push drugs during compressions (never stopping compressions to give one), and never use direct venipuncture in the field because of infiltration risk.
points.zh: IV 是最快也最危险的途径：整剂量一次性进入体内，正常情况下血药浓度均衡约需 30-60 秒；但心脏骤停 CPR 期间，药物到达靶器官要慢 3-4 倍，因为此时心排出量只有正常的约三分之一——要等至少 1-2 分钟才能判断药效，应在按压间隙推药（绝不能为了给药而中断按压），现场也绝不能用直接静脉穿刺给药，因为有药液外渗的风险。

points.en: IO is considered as fast and effective as IV — sometimes better — because the medication enters a noncollapsible venous channel with rapid flow straight into central circulation; anything that can be given IV can be given IO.
points.zh: IO（骨髓腔内）被认为和 IV 一样快、一样有效——有时甚至更好——因为药物进入的是一条不会塌陷的血管通道，能快速直达中央循环；凡是能 IV 给的药，都能 IO 给。

points.en: IM injection is slower in onset than IV (must first be absorbed from muscle into blood) but has a longer duration of action, absorbed gradually over minutes to hours; it requires adequate perfusion (avoid in shock/cardiac arrest) and is typically 1-5 mL into the deltoid (preferred prehospital site, and easy to slow absorption with a proximal tourniquet if an allergic reaction develops) or the upper-outer gluteal quadrant.
points.zh: 肌肉注射起效比 IV 慢（要先从肌肉吸收进血液），但作用时间更长，在数分钟到数小时内缓慢吸收；需要有足够灌注（休克/心脏骤停时避免使用），通常打 1-5 mL 到三角肌（院前首选部位，一旦出现过敏反应还能在近端扎止血带减慢吸收）或臀部外上象限。

points.en: SC injection is usually under 2 mL into subcutaneous fat/connective tissue, absorbed more slowly and over a longer period than IV, with peak effect around 30 minutes; typical sites are the upper outer arm, anterior thigh, or abdomen — it can be used for epinephrine in mild-to-moderate asthma, though IM is preferred.
points.zh: 皮下注射通常不到 2 mL，打进皮下脂肪/结缔组织，吸收比 IV 慢、持续时间更长，峰值效果约在 30 分钟；常用部位是上臂外侧、大腿前侧或腹部——轻中度哮喘发作时可用皮下给肾上腺素，但更推荐肌注。

sections.titleZh: 药代动力学：吸收、分布、生物转化与排泄

points.en: Pharmacokinetics studies how the body handles a drug over time — absorption, distribution, biotransformation (metabolism), and excretion. Drugs cross cell membranes by active transport (energy-dependent, carrier-mediated, can move against the concentration gradient) or passive diffusion (no energy needed, high-to-low concentration; lipid-soluble drugs cross membranes directly, water-soluble ones through aqueous channels).
points.zh: 药代动力学研究身体如何随时间处理一种药——吸收、分布、生物转化（代谢）、排泄。药物跨越细胞膜靠主动转运（耗能、需要载体，能逆浓度梯度移动）或被动扩散（不耗能，从高浓度到低浓度；脂溶性药直接穿膜，水溶性药走水性通道）。

points.en: Absorption speed rises with better regional blood flow (rich vascular sites absorb faster; shock or poor perfusion slows any route), larger absorbing surface area, and single-layer tissue (intestine) versus multilayer tissue (skin, which is slower).
points.zh: 吸收速度会因局部血流更好而提高（血管丰富的部位吸收更快；休克或灌注差会拖慢任何途径），吸收面积越大也越快，单层组织（肠道）比多层组织（皮肤，更慢）吸收得快。

points.en: Continuous therapy typically uses a loading dose (a large dose, sized to the volume of distribution/patient weight, that temporarily exceeds elimination capacity to reach a therapeutic level fast) followed by a maintenance dose (smaller, sized to the body's elimination rate, to hold that level).
points.zh: 持续治疗通常先给负荷剂量（一次较大剂量，按分布容积/体重估算，暂时超过身体的清除能力，目的是快速达到治疗浓度），再给维持剂量（较小剂量，按身体清除速度估算，用来维持这个浓度）。

points.en: Most drugs are weak acids or weak bases and ionize to a degree set by the surrounding pH — weak acids ionize better in an alkaline environment, weak bases ionize better in an acidic one. Bioavailability is how much of the administered dose is still chemically active by the time it reaches the target organ.
points.zh: 大多数药物是弱酸或弱碱，电离程度由所处 pH 决定——弱酸在碱性环境电离更充分，弱碱在酸性环境电离更充分。生物利用度是指给药剂量中，真正到达靶器官时仍具活性的那部分比例。

points.en: Distribution depends on cardiac output and regional blood flow (e.g. cold shunts blood away from skin, delaying a drug meant for a foot infection). Only free (unbound) drug is active — drugs bind reversibly to plasma proteins (mainly albumin) and are stored in fat, muscle, and bone, with lipid-soluble drugs accumulating heavily in fat, especially when blood flow is low; free and bound drug stay in a fixed proportion, so as free drug is used up, bound drug releases more to replace it.
points.zh: 分布取决于心排出量和局部血流（例如受寒时血液从皮肤分流出去，会延迟本该送到脚部感染灶的药）。只有游离（未结合）的药物才有活性——药物会可逆地结合血浆蛋白（主要是白蛋白），也会储存在脂肪、肌肉和骨骼里，脂溶性药物在血流低时尤其容易大量堆积在脂肪中；游离药和结合药始终保持固定比例，所以游离药被用掉后，结合的部分会释放出更多来补充。

points.en: The blood-brain barrier (a single layer of capillary endothelium) and the placental barrier (membrane layers between maternal and fetal blood) both restrict passage mostly to lipid-soluble drugs — neither barrier is absolute, so some non-lipid-soluble drugs can still cross.
points.zh: 血脑屏障（单层毛细血管内皮细胞）和胎盘屏障（母体与胎儿血液之间的膜层）大致都只让脂溶性药物通过——但两者都不是绝对屏障，仍有部分非脂溶性药物能穿过去。

points.en: Biotransformation happens mostly in the liver (hepatocyte endoplasmic-reticulum enzymes), only on free drug, in two phases: Phase 1 (oxidation or hydrolysis, increasing water solubility) then Phase 2 (conjugation with a body chemical) before excretion; prodrugs are inactive until biotransformation activates them.
points.zh: 生物转化主要发生在肝脏（肝细胞内质网上的酶），只作用于游离药物，分两个阶段：第一阶段（氧化或水解，提高水溶性），再进入第二阶段（与体内某种化学物质结合，即结合反应）后才排泄；前药（prodrug）要经过生物转化才会被激活。

points.en: The first-pass effect: all blood absorbed from the GI tract passes through the liver before reaching the rest of the body, so the liver can partially or completely inactivate a drug before it ever reaches its target — insulin must therefore always be given parenterally (SC), never orally, because the liver would destroy it; some other drugs simply need a higher oral dose to compensate for first-pass loss.
points.zh: 首过效应：从消化道吸收的血液在进入全身循环前必须先经过肝脏，肝脏可能在药物到达靶器官之前就把它部分或完全灭活——所以胰岛素必须走肠外途径（皮下）给药，绝不能口服，否则会被肝脏破坏；其他一些药物只是需要更高的口服剂量来抵消首过效应造成的损失。

points.en: Excretion is mainly renal, via three mechanisms — glomerular filtration (passive, pressure-driven), tubular secretion (active transport), and partial reabsorption (some filtered drug is reabsorbed back) — and, just as with absorption, urine pH affects excretion speed: the closer a drug's pH is to the urine's pH, the slower it is excreted.
points.zh: 排泄主要经肾脏完成，靠三种机制——肾小球滤过（被动、靠压力差）、肾小管分泌（主动转运）、部分重吸收（部分被滤出的药又被重新吸收回去）——和吸收一样，尿液 pH 也会影响排泄速度：药物 pH 和尿液 pH 越接近，排泄就越慢。

sections.titleEn: Pharmacodynamics: Receptor Theory, Half-Life, and Drug Responses
sections.titleZh: 药效动力学：受体理论、半衰期与药物反应

points.en: Pharmacodynamics is how a drug produces its intended effect (mechanism of action) plus the factors that alter that response. Four action mechanisms exist: binding a receptor site (most common in EMS), changing a cell's physical properties (e.g. osmotic balance), chemically combining with other substances, or altering a normal metabolic pathway.
points.zh: 药效动力学研究药物如何产生预期效果（作用机制）以及哪些因素会改变这个反应。共有四种作用机制：结合受体位点（EMS 中最常见）、改变细胞的物理性质（如渗透压平衡）、与其他物质发生化学结合、或改变正常代谢通路。

points.en: A drug binding a receptor is an agonist if it triggers the receptor's normal response, an antagonist if it blocks that response, or a partial agonist/agonist-antagonist if it does both; winning the receptor requires higher affinity than the natural mediator or any competing drug. Prolonged binding can down-regulate (reduce) available receptors, while some drugs up-regulate (increase) them.
points.zh: 药物结合受体后，若触发受体的正常反应就是激动剂，若阻断该反应就是拮抗剂，若两者都有则是部分激动剂/激动-拮抗剂；要抢到受体，亲和力必须高于天然介质或任何竞争药物。长期占据受体可能导致下调（受体数量减少），也有药物会导致上调（受体数量增加）。

points.en: Plasma-profile timeline: onset of action (time to reach the minimum effective concentration at the target), duration of action (time spent above that minimum), and termination of action (time from falling below the minimum to full elimination).
points.zh: 血浆浓度时间线：起效时间（达到靶部位最低有效浓度所需时间）、作用持续时间（浓度维持在最低有效浓度以上的时间）、终止时间（浓度跌破最低有效值到完全清除所需时间）。

points.en: Therapeutic index = LD50 (the dose lethal to 50% of the population) divided by ED50 (the dose effective in 50% of the population) — a larger ratio means a wider margin of safety. Biologic half-life is the time required for the body to eliminate half of the drug present.
points.zh: 治疗指数＝LD50（对 50% 人群致命的剂量）除以 ED50（对 50% 人群有效的剂量）——比值越大，安全边际越宽。生物半衰期是指身体清除体内一半药量所需要的时间。

points.en: Weight-based dosing: reference formulations assume a 70-kg adult, but the same dose produces very different blood concentrations in, say, a 48-kg versus a 136-kg patient — emergency dosing therefore is usually expressed in milligrams per kilogram of the patient's actual body weight (mg/kg) to correct for this.
points.zh: 按体重给药：参考剂量通常按 70 kg 成人设定，但同一剂量在 48 kg 和 136 kg 病人体内产生的血药浓度会差很多——所以急救给药通常用「每公斤体重多少毫克」（mg/kg）来表达剂量，以校正这个差异。

points.en: Other response variables: age (elderly patients are generally more drug-sensitive and need lower doses, though some drugs like barbiturates can paradoxically agitate rather than sedate older patients), sex, environment, timing relative to meals/exercise (food slows oral onset), the patient's own condition (renal failure lets drug levels build toward toxicity; shock can delay injected-drug absorption for hours; hypothermia can make a drug ineffective until the patient rewarms), genetics (enzyme deficiency slows drug handling), and psychological factors (the placebo effect — a fake medication can still produce real physiologic effects).
points.zh: 其他影响反应的变量：年龄（老年人普遍对药物更敏感、需要更低剂量，但巴比妥类等少数药在老年人身上反而可能引起躁动而非镇静）、性别、环境、用药时机（进食会延缓口服起效，运动或空腹则相反）、病人自身状况（肾衰竭会让药物在体内蓄积到中毒水平；休克可能让注射药物延迟数小时才被吸收；低体温会让药物在复温前失效）、遗传因素（酶缺乏会拖慢药物代谢）、以及心理因素（安慰剂效应——假药也能产生真实的生理反应）。

points.en: Every drug has some side effect (even oxygen); whether to give it comes down to the risk-benefit ratio. An iatrogenic response is harm caused by the treatment itself (e.g. a UTI from an indwelling catheter). An allergic reaction is an unpredictable hypersensitivity response that can progress to anaphylaxis; an idiosyncrasy is a response unique to one particular patient, not seen in others.
points.zh: 每种药都有副作用（连氧气都有）；给不给要看风险-收益比。医源性反应是治疗本身造成的伤害（例如留置导尿管引起的尿路感染）。过敏反应是不可预测的超敏反应，可能进展成过敏性休克；特异质反应是只发生在某个特定病人身上、别人身上看不到的独特反应。

points.en: Tolerance (decreased response to repeated doses of the same drug, needing higher doses over time), cross-tolerance (tolerance carried over from a related drug — e.g. chronic oxycodone use blunts the response to morphine), and tachyphylaxis (tolerance developing rapidly, sometimes after just a couple of doses, classically with sympathomimetics) are three related but distinct patterns; a cumulative effect (repeated doses stacking up in a short time) and drug dependence (withdrawal symptoms on stopping) are separate concepts again.
points.zh: 耐受性（反复用同一种药后反应减弱，需要越来越高的剂量）、交叉耐受（对一种药的耐受延伸到相关药物上——例如长期用羟考酮会削弱对吗啡的反应）、快速减敏（耐受产生得很快，有时只要两剂就出现，典型见于拟交感药）是三种相关但不同的模式；蓄积效应（短时间内多剂叠加）和药物依赖（停药后出现戒断症状）则是另外两个独立概念。

points.en: When two drugs interact: summation is a simple additive effect (response equals the sum of both); synergism is when the combined response exceeds that simple sum; potentiation is when one drug boosts another's effect (e.g. alcohol taken with acetaminophen drives more acetaminophen into the liver, raising acute liver-failure risk — alcohol-acetaminophen syndrome); interference is a direct biochemical interaction between two drugs, and one drug can also be used deliberately to block another's receptor effect (e.g. naloxone reversing morphine).
points.zh: 两药相互作用的类型：相加是简单叠加（反应等于两者之和）；协同是合并反应超过简单相加之和；增强是一种药放大另一种药的效果（例如酒精和对乙酰氨基酚同服，会把更多对乙酰氨基酚推入肝脏，增加急性肝衰竭风险，即「酒精-对乙酰氨基酚综合征」）；干扰是两药之间直接的生化相互作用；也可以刻意利用一种药去阻断另一种药的受体效应（如纳洛酮逆转吗啡）。

sections.titleEn: Medication Storage and the Medication Profile
sections.titleZh: 药物储存与药物专论的构成

points.en: Most medications degrade with heat, direct sunlight, or humidity; the general storage range is about 15°C to 30°C, out of direct sunlight, per each manufacturer's guidance. Controlled substances need a securely locked, opaque (not glass/plastic), unmarked cabinet, plus a disposition record documenting every use, wasted amount, and return of expired stock.
points.zh: 大多数药物会因高温、日晒或潮湿而降解；一般储存范围约为 15°C 至 30°C，避免阳光直射，具体以厂商说明为准。管制药物需要锁在牢固、不透明（不能是玻璃或塑料材质）、不带标识的柜子里，还要有处置记录，记下每一次使用量、废弃量和过期药品的退回情况。

points.en: A full medication profile has nine standard components: names (chemical/generic/trade), classification, mechanism of action, indications, pharmacokinetics (route-specific onset and duration), side/adverse effects, routes of administration, dosage forms and concentrations, dosages (weight/age-adjusted), contraindications, and special-population considerations — knowing a drug's classification is what makes memorizing all of this manageable.
points.zh: 一份完整的药物专论有九个标准组成部分：药名（化学名/通用名/商品名）、分类、作用机制、适应证、药代动力学（不同途径的起效和持续时间）、副作用/不良反应、给药途径、剂型与浓度、剂量（按体重/年龄调整）、禁忌证，以及特殊人群注意事项——知道一种药的分类，正是让记住这一大堆信息变得可管理的关键。

sections.titleZh: 肾上腺素能/胆碱能受体、镇痛药与支气管扩张药

points.en: Four adrenergic receptor types by effect: Alpha-1 (peripheral vasoconstriction, mild bronchoconstriction, raises metabolism), Alpha-2 (controls norepinephrine release), Beta-1 (raises heart rate, contractility, automaticity, and conduction velocity), Beta-2 (vasodilation and bronchodilation). Dopaminergic receptors dilate the renal, coronary, and cerebral arteries when stimulated, but no medication targets them selectively.
points.zh: 四种肾上腺素能受体及其效应：α1（外周血管收缩、轻度支气管收缩、加快代谢）、α2（控制去甲肾上腺素的释放）、β1（提高心率、收缩力、自律性和传导速度）、β2（血管扩张和支气管扩张）。多巴胺能受体被激活时会扩张肾、冠状和脑动脉，但目前没有专门靶向它的药物。

points.en: Clinical logic follows directly from the receptors: beta-1 agonism treats cardiac arrest/hypotension by raising contractility, while beta-1 antagonism lowers heart rate/conduction to treat tachycardia; beta-2 agonism relieves bronchospasm in asthma (beta-2 antagonism has no clinical use — we never want bronchoconstriction); alpha-1 agonism raises blood pressure via preload/afterload, while alpha-1 antagonism lowers it but triggers a reflex response (faster heart rate, renal sodium/water retention) as the body tries to compensate.
points.zh: 临床用药逻辑直接来自受体本身：激动 β1 用于心脏骤停/低血压，靠提高收缩力；拮抗 β1 则降低心率和传导速度，用于治疗心动过速；激动 β2 能缓解哮喘的支气管痉挛（拮抗 β2 没有任何临床用途——我们从不希望支气管收缩）；激动 α1 靠提高前负荷/后负荷升高血压，拮抗 α1 则降压，但会触发身体的反射性代偿（心率加快、肾脏保钠保水）。

points.en: Nicotinic receptors sit at all autonomic ganglia and neuromuscular junctions; muscarinic receptors are widespread and carry most of the parasympathetic response. Excess cholinergic stimulation (from organophosphate pesticides or nerve agents like VX or sarin) produces the SLUDGEM toxidrome: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI upset, Emesis, Miosis.
points.zh: 烟碱型受体分布在所有自主神经节和神经肌肉接头；毒蕈碱型受体分布广泛，承担大部分副交感反应。有机磷农药或神经毒剂（VX、沙林）造成的胆碱能过度刺激，会产生 SLUDGEM 中毒综合征：流涎（Salivation）、流泪（Lacrimation）、排尿（Urination）、排便（Defecation）、胃肠不适（GI upset）、呕吐（Emesis）、瞳孔缩小（Miosis）。

points.en: Anticholinergic drugs block muscarinic receptors — atropine, for example, decreases secretions, raises heart rate, dilates pupils, and slows GI activity; blocking nicotinic receptors instead would disable the entire ANS, so that is essentially never done therapeutically.
points.zh: 抗胆碱药阻断毒蕈碱型受体——例如阿托品，能减少分泌物、提高心率、扩瞳、减慢胃肠活动；如果阻断的是烟碱型受体，会直接让整个自主神经系统失能，所以治疗上基本不这么用。

points.en: Opioid agonists remain the mainstay of prehospital analgesia, binding opiate receptors to block pain signals while also depressing the CNS; fentanyl is popular for fast, short action (analgesia within about 90 seconds, lasting about 30 minutes), while morphine additionally lowers cardiac preload/afterload — and therefore myocardial oxygen demand — giving it a specific role in cardiac chest pain.
points.zh: 阿片类激动剂仍是院前镇痛的主力，通过结合阿片受体阻断痛觉信号，同时抑制中枢神经系统；芬太尼因起效快、作用短而受欢迎（约 90 秒起效，持续约 30 分钟），吗啡则额外能降低心脏前负荷/后负荷——从而降低心肌氧耗——这也是它在心源性胸痛中有特殊地位的原因。

points.en: Nonopioid analgesics act through prostaglandin/COX pathways and fall into three families — salicylates (aspirin), NSAIDs (ibuprofen), and para-aminophenol derivatives (acetaminophen) — many doubling as antipyretics. Opioid antagonists (naloxone) competitively occupy opiate receptors without activating them, physically blocking opioid molecules from binding there.
points.zh: 非阿片类镇痛药通过前列腺素/COX 通路起效，分三大家族——水杨酸类（阿司匹林）、NSAID（布洛芬）、对氨基酚衍生物（对乙酰氨基酚）——很多同时兼具退热作用。阿片拮抗剂（纳洛酮）会竞争性占据阿片受体但不激活它，物理性地挡住阿片分子结合。

points.en: Aspirin's COX selectivity is the classic exam trap: aspirin targets COX-1 to reduce platelet aggregation (useful in suspected MI), while ibuprofen targets COX-2 far more — so ibuprofen is NOT an acceptable substitute for aspirin in suspected ACS, even though both are technically NSAID-family drugs.
points.zh: 阿司匹林对 COX 的选择性是经典考点：阿司匹林靶向 COX-1 来抑制血小板聚集（对疑似心梗有用），而布洛芬更多靶向 COX-2——所以疑似 ACS 时不能用布洛芬代替阿司匹林，尽管两者都算 NSAID 家族。

points.en: Beta-2-selective sympathomimetic bronchodilators (e.g. salbutamol) are preferred over nonselective sympathomimetics in respiratory emergencies, because nonselective agents also hit beta-1 and raise heart rate/oxygen demand exactly when oxygen is already short; xanthines and inhaled/systemic corticosteroids serve as second-line respiratory treatments (relaxing bronchial smooth muscle, or suppressing airway inflammation, respectively).
points.zh: 呼吸急症首选 β2 选择性拟交感支气管扩张药（如沙丁胺醇），而不是非选择性拟交感药，因为非选择性药物也会激动 β1，在氧本就不够的时候还进一步提高心率和耗氧；黄嘌呤类和吸入/全身皮质类固醇是二线呼吸用药（分别通过松弛支气管平滑肌、抑制气道炎症起效）。

points.en: General anesthesia, deep sedation/hypnosis, and neuromuscular blockade (paralytics) sit mostly outside BC's PCP scope of practice — they belong to physician/ACP-level advanced airway management. The one concept worth carrying forward: these drugs are graded by onset/duration (e.g. succinylcholine, the standard rapid-sequence paralytic, has an onset under 45 seconds and a duration of only 4-5 minutes), and a failed intubation attempt on a long-acting paralytic can leave a patient without spontaneous breathing for up to an hour.
points.zh: 全身麻醉、深度镇静/催眠和神经肌肉阻滞（麻痹剂）大多不在 BC PCP 的执业范围内——它们属于医生/ACP 级别的高级气道管理。唯一值得带走的概念是：这类药按起效/持续时间分级（例如快速诱导插管标准用药琥珀胆碱，起效不到 45 秒，只持续 4-5 分钟），而如果用了长效麻痹剂却插管失败，病人可能长达一小时没有自主呼吸。

sections.titleEn: Cardiovascular, Coagulation, GI, and Endocrine/OB Drugs
sections.titleZh: 心血管、凝血、消化与内分泌/产科用药

points.en: Three cardiac drug-effect terms — chronotropic (heart-rate effect), inotropic (force-of-contraction effect), dromotropic (conduction-velocity effect) — can each be positive or negative, and a single drug can move each axis differently: digoxin, for example, is positively inotropic but modestly negatively chronotropic and more dramatically negatively dromotropic.
points.zh: 三个心脏用药效应术语——变时性（心率效应）、变力性（收缩力效应）、变传导性（传导速度效应）——各自可正可负，同一种药在三个轴上的方向可能不一样：例如地高辛，正性变力，但轻度负性变时、更明显的负性变传导。

points.en: The four antidysrhythmic classes by mechanism: Class 1 sodium-channel blockers (slow conduction, negative dromotropic), Class 2 beta blockers (reduce adrenergic beta stimulation), Class 3 potassium-channel blockers (increase contractility, prevent re-entry), Class 4 calcium-channel blockers (reduce contractile force and automaticity, also negative dromotropic).
points.zh: 四类抗心律失常药按作用机制划分：I 类钠通道阻滞剂（减慢传导，负性变传导）、II 类 β 受体阻滞剂（降低肾上腺素能 β 刺激）、III 类钾通道阻滞剂（增强收缩力，阻止折返）、IV 类钙通道阻滞剂（降低收缩力和自律性，也是负性变传导）。

points.en: Nearly a quarter of Canadian adults have hypertension (24% of men, 23% of women). Antihypertensive families include diuretics (thiazides control renal sodium/water; loop diuretics lower sodium/calcium but risk hypokalemia), vasodilators (e.g. nitroglycerin — vessel dilation triggers a reflex sympathetic response, which is why vasodilator therapy is often paired with a sympathetic blocker), beta blockers/adrenergic inhibitors, ACE inhibitors (block angiotensin I to angiotensin II conversion) and angiotensin-II receptor blockers, and calcium channel blockers (dilate coronary arteries and reduce peripheral vascular resistance).
points.zh: 将近四分之一的加拿大成年人有高血压（男性 24%，女性 23%）。抗高血压药家族包括利尿剂（噻嗪类控制肾脏钠/水排出；袢利尿剂降低钠/钙但有低钾风险）、血管扩张药（如硝酸甘油——血管扩张会触发反射性交感兴奋，这也是血管扩张药常常要搭配交感阻滞药一起用的原因）、β 受体阻滞剂/肾上腺素能抑制剂、ACE 抑制剂（阻断血管紧张素 I 转为 II）和血管紧张素 II 受体阻滞剂，以及钙通道阻滞剂（扩张冠状动脉、降低外周血管阻力）。

points.en: Coagulation-system drugs: antiplatelet agents (aspirin via COX-1; newer P2Y12 blockers clopidogrel/prasugrel/ticagrelor) prevent platelet aggregation but don't break down existing clots; anticoagulants (heparin/LMWH bind and potentiate antithrombin; warfarin instead blocks vitamin-K-dependent clotting-factor synthesis and is reversed by vitamin K) prevent new clot formation but also blunt the clotting needed to stop traumatic bleeding — always ask about anticoagulant use in a trauma patient.
points.zh: 凝血系统用药：抗血小板药（阿司匹林经 COX-1；新一代 P2Y12 阻滞剂氯吡格雷/普拉格雷/替格瑞洛）阻止血小板聚集，但不会分解已形成的血栓；抗凝药（肝素/低分子肝素结合并增强抗凝血酶的作用；华法林则是阻断维生素 K 依赖性凝血因子的合成，可用维生素 K 逆转）阻止新血栓形成，但也会削弱止住外伤出血所需的凝血能力——创伤病人一定要问抗凝药史。

points.en: DOACs (direct thrombin inhibitor dabigatran; direct factor Xa inhibitors rivaroxaban/apixaban/edoxaban) need far less lab monitoring than warfarin, but only dabigatran currently has a Canadian-approved reversal agent (idarucizumab). Fibrinolytics (tissue plasminogen activator, tenecteplase) dissolve an already-formed clot; TXA works the opposite way — it inhibits fibrinolysis to stabilize clots already formed, which is why it helps in massive traumatic hemorrhage rather than in ACS or stroke.
points.zh: 新型口服抗凝药（直接凝血酶抑制剂达比加群；直接 Xa 因子抑制剂利伐沙班/阿哌沙班/依度沙班）比华法林需要的实验室监测少得多，但目前只有达比加群在加拿大有获批的逆转剂（依达赛珠单抗）。溶栓药（组织型纤溶酶原激活物、替奈普酶）溶解已形成的血栓；TXA 则反其道而行——抑制纤维蛋白溶解来稳定已形成的血凝块，这也是它在大量创伤性出血中有用、而不是用在 ACS 或卒中的原因。

points.en: GI: antiemetics (dimenhydrinate is classified as both an antihistamine and an antiemetic, blocking H1 receptors; others include promethazine, prochlorperazine, metoclopramide, ondansetron) treat nausea/vomiting; the broader GI-agent family includes antacids, H2-blockers/proton pump inhibitors for acid, laxatives, and antidiarrheals — patients commonly take these even though paramedics rarely administer any but the antiemetics.
points.zh: 消化系统：止吐药（茶苯海明兼具抗组胺和止吐分类，阻断 H1 受体；其他还有异丙嗪、丙氯拉嗪、甲氧氯普胺、昂丹司琼）用于治疗恶心呕吐；更广的消化系统用药家族还包括抗酸药、H2 阻滞剂/质子泵抑制剂（控制胃酸）、泻药和止泻药——病人常在服用这些，但急救员通常只给止吐药。

points.en: Practical exam trap: ask every chest-pain patient about erectile-dysfunction medication (sildenafil, vardenafil, tadalafil) before giving nitroglycerin — combining a phosphodiesterase inhibitor with a vasodilator within 24-48 hours of the last dose can cause profound, refractory, life-threatening hypotension.
points.zh: 实操考经典陷阱：给硝酸甘油前一定要问所有胸痛病人有没有吃过治疗勃起功能障碍的药（西地那非、伐地那非、他达拉非）——磷酸二酯酶抑制剂在最后一次服药后 24-48 小时内和血管扩张药合用，可能造成难以纠正、危及生命的严重低血压。

points.en: OB drugs: oxytocin is the only HPFB-approved medication to augment labour, and it also treats postpartum hemorrhage by increasing uterine contraction force/frequency; tocolytics suppress labour when it starts too early or endangers mother/baby — magnesium sulfate (relaxes smooth muscle including the uterus) is the most common, with terbutaline (a beta agonist) as an alternative.
points.zh: 产科用药：缩宫素是唯一获 HPFB 核准用来加强产程的药物，也通过增强子宫收缩力和频率来治疗产后出血；宫缩抑制剂在产程过早启动或危及母婴时用来抑制宫缩——最常用的是硫酸镁（松弛平滑肌，包括子宫），特布他林（一种 β 受体激动剂）是替代选择。

points.en: Give thiamine (vitamin B1) IV before or with dextrose in a patient at risk of thiamine deficiency (e.g. alcohol use disorder), because thiamine is required to metabolize the incoming carbohydrate load effectively — corticosteroids (e.g. dexamethasone, methylprednisolone) are the other endocrine-adjacent drug family worth knowing, used to suppress inflammation in both respiratory emergencies and adrenal-cortex disorders.
points.zh: 对有硫胺素（维生素 B1）缺乏风险的病人（如酒精使用障碍），给葡萄糖前或同时要先给硫胺素 IV，因为身体要靠硫胺素才能有效代谢随之而来的碳水化合物负荷——皮质类固醇（如地塞米松、甲泼尼龙）是另一个值得记住的内分泌相关药物家族，用于抑制呼吸急症和肾上腺皮质疾病中的炎症反应。

points.en: Antidotes work by one of three mechanisms: blocking the receptor the toxin would otherwise stimulate, converting the toxic agent into an inert form to ease excretion, or binding the agent to prevent its absorption into the bloodstream — naloxone (the prehospital opioid antagonist) is the clearest everyday example of the first mechanism.
points.zh: 解毒剂通过三种机制之一起效：阻断毒物本该刺激的受体、把毒性物质转化成惰性形式以便排出，或者结合毒物阻止它被吸收进血液——纳洛酮（院前用的阿片拮抗剂）就是第一种机制最典型的日常例子。

sections.titleEn: The BC Correspondence Table: 12 PCP Classifications to Named Drugs
sections.titleZh: BC 对照表：12 个 PCP 分类 ↔ 具名药物

points.en: All 12 PCP written-exam classifications map onto at least one of BC's 18 named drugs (see the full correspondence table in hardNumbers) — two classifications, Antiemetic and Carbohydrate, each map to two different BC drugs, so a written-exam question naming that one classification could be testing the mechanism/route of either drug behind it.
points.zh: PCP 笔试的 12 个分类，每一个都至少对应 BC 18 份药物专论里的一款药（完整对照表见 hardNumbers）——其中止吐药（Antiemetic）和碳水化合物（Carbohydrate）这两个分类各自对应两款不同的 BC 药，所以笔试题目点名这两个分类时，考的可能是背后任何一款药的机制或途径。

points.en: Antiemetic covers both dimenhydrinate (IM/IV, 1 mg/kg to a maximum of 50 mg) and ondansetron (PO, 4 mg); Carbohydrate covers both D10W (IV, 10-25 g) and oral glucose (PO, 15 g). Their routes, doses, and onset times differ sharply even though the PCP written exam would call both members of each pair by the exact same one-word classification label.
points.zh: 止吐药同时涵盖茶苯海明（IM/IV，1 mg/kg，最大 50 mg）和昂丹司琼（口服，4 mg）；碳水化合物同时涵盖 D10W（静脉，10-25 g）和口服葡萄糖（口服，15 g）。这两组药各自的途径、剂量和起效时间差别很大，尽管 PCP 笔试对同组里的两款药会用完全相同的一个分类词来称呼。

points.en: Four of BC's 18 named drugs carry NO COPR PCP classification at all — dexamethasone, Entonox (nitrous oxide), methoxyflurane (Penthrox), and TXA — so these exist purely at the BC EMALB practical/licensing layer and will never appear, even indirectly, on the PCP written paper by classification; they still must be known by name, dose, and route for the practical station.
points.zh: BC 18 份药物专论里有 4 款完全没有 COPR PCP 分类——地塞米松、Entonox（一氧化二氮/笑气）、甲氧氟烷（Penthrox）和 TXA——这几款药只存在于 BC EMALB 实操/执照考这一层，PCP 笔试哪怕间接也不会考它们的分类；但实操站仍然要求你知道它们的名字、剂量和途径。

points.en: Ten classifications map one-to-one and are worth memorizing as fixed pairs: Platelet inhibitor = aspirin, Antihistamine = diphenhydramine, Sympathomimetic = epinephrine, Antihypoglycemic hormone = glucagon, Nonnarcotic analgesic = acetaminophen, NSAID = ibuprofen, Anticholinergic bronchodilator = ipratropium, Opioid antagonist = naloxone, Vasodilator = nitroglycerin, Sympathomimetic bronchodilator = salbutamol.
points.zh: 另外十个分类是一对一的固定搭配，直接背下来就行：血小板抑制剂＝阿司匹林，抗组胺药＝苯海拉明，拟交感药＝肾上腺素，抗低血糖激素＝胰高血糖素，非麻醉性镇痛药＝对乙酰氨基酚，NSAID＝布洛芬，抗胆碱能支气管扩张药＝异丙托溴铵，阿片拮抗剂＝纳洛酮，血管扩张药＝硝酸甘油，拟交感支气管扩张药＝沙丁胺醇。

points.en: Study workflow: for the PCP written paper, memorize classification-to-mechanism logic (e.g. 'a vasodilator relaxes arteriolar/venous smooth muscle' — never the word nitroglycerin); for the practical station and licensing exam, flip around and memorize name-to-dose/route/onset/contraindication from each full monograph in drugs.json.
points.zh: 备考方式：PCP 笔试要背「分类→机制」的逻辑（例如「血管扩张药会松弛小动脉/静脉平滑肌」——永远不会出现「硝酸甘油」这个词）；实操站和执照考则要反过来，把 drugs.json 里每一款药的完整专论背成「药名→剂量/途径/起效/禁忌」。

sections.titleEn: Tying It Together: Reading Home Meds and Dose-Calculation Formulas
sections.titleZh: 综合运用：读懂居家用药与剂量计算公式

points.en: A patient's medication list is a diagnostic shortcut: a spilled bottle of nitroglycerin next to an unresponsive patient narrows the differential toward cardiac disease before you even finish the physical exam, and a home-med list can be more reliable than the patient's own self-report (e.g. a patient who denies hypertension but is taking labetalol — a beta blocker specifically used to treat it).
points.zh: 病人的用药清单是一条诊断捷径：在无反应病人身边发现撒了一地的硝酸甘油药瓶，还没做完体查就能把鉴别诊断收窄到心脏疾病；用药清单有时比病人自己说的病史更可靠（例如病人说自己没有高血压，却在吃拉贝洛尔——一种专门用来治高血压的 β 受体阻滞剂）。

points.en: Home medications can hide the classic presentation of a condition: a patient in hypovolemic shock should show tachycardia before hypotension, but a patient on a beta blocker may not be able to mount that compensatory tachycardia at all — silently removing the earliest warning sign of shock.
points.zh: 居家用药可能掩盖一种病情的经典表现：低血容量性休克的病人本该先出现心动过速再出现低血压，但正在服用 β 受体阻滞剂的病人可能根本无法产生这种代偿性心动过速——悄悄抹掉了休克最早的警示信号。

points.en: Worked case pattern: digoxin toxicity classically causes visual disturbance (blurred vision, yellow-green halos around objects) alongside bradycardia/dysrhythmia; a calcium channel blocker like diltiazem can potentiate digoxin by raising its blood level, and calcium chloride is the specific reversal treatment for calcium-channel-blocker toxicity.
points.zh: 病例套路：地高辛中毒的经典表现是视觉障碍（视物模糊、物体周围出现黄绿色光晕）合并心动过缓/心律失常；地尔硫卓这类钙通道阻滞剂可能通过升高地高辛血药浓度而增强其毒性（潜化），而氯化钙是钙通道阻滞剂中毒的特异性逆转治疗。

points.en: Therapeutic-index intuition: the closer LD50/ED50 is to 1, the more dangerous the drug, because the gap between an effective dose and a lethal dose is razor-thin — digoxin is the textbook example, which is why patients on it need regular blood-level checks.
points.zh: 治疗指数的直觉理解：LD50÷ED50 越接近 1，这种药就越危险，因为有效剂量和致死剂量之间的差距薄如刀锋——地高辛就是教材级的例子，这也是为什么用地高辛的病人要定期查血药浓度。

points.en: Three reusable dose-calculation formulas: weight-based dose (mg) = patient weight (kg) x ordered dose (mg/kg); volume to draw up (mL) = desired dose (mg) / concentration (mg/mL); IV drip rate (gtt/min) = [volume (mL) x drop factor (gtts/mL)] / time (min).
points.zh: 三个可以直接套用的剂量计算公式：按体重给药剂量（mg）＝病人体重（kg）×医嘱剂量（mg/kg）；要抽取的体积（mL）＝目标剂量（mg）÷药物浓度（mg/mL）；静脉滴速（gtt/min）＝〔总体积（mL）×点滴系数（gtts/mL）〕÷输注时间（min）。

points.en: Worked check against a real BC monograph: acetaminophen's own IV instructions call for a 1,000 mg/100 mL bag run over 15 minutes on a standard 10 gtts/mL set — plugging that into the drip-rate formula gives (100 mL x 10 gtts/mL) / 15 min = about 66 gtt/min, exactly the number BC's own monograph states.
points.zh: 用真实的 BC 专论验算一遍：对乙酰氨基酚的静脉给药说明是「1,000 mg/100 mL 药袋，用标准 10 gtts/mL 输液器在 15 分钟内输完」——代入滴速公式：（100 mL×10 gtts/mL）÷15 min≈66 gtt/min，正好和 BC 专论里写的数字对上。

atScene.en: Before administering any medication, echo back the order out loud and match the drug's packaging against what was ordered — the wrong-drug error is the single most common medication mistake, and this ten-second habit catches most of them before the needle goes in.
atScene.zh: 给任何药之前，先大声复述一遍医嘱，并核对药物包装和医嘱是否一致——给错药是最常见的单一用药错误，这个十秒钟的习惯能在扎针前挡下大多数错误。

atScene.en: In cardiac arrest, draw up medications ahead of time, push them during compression cycles rather than pausing compressions, and remember the drug will take 3-4 times longer than normal to reach its target because CPR-generated cardiac output is only about a third of normal — do not judge the drug a failure before at least 1-2 minutes have passed.
atScene.zh: 心脏骤停时，提前把药抽好，在按压间隙推药、不要为了给药暂停按压，并记住 CPR 下药物到达靶器官要比平时慢 3-4 倍，因为此时的心排出量只有正常的约三分之一——至少等 1-2 分钟再判断这剂药是不是没效。

atScene.en: Before giving nitroglycerin to any chest-pain patient, specifically ask about erectile-dysfunction medication use in the last 24-48 hours — the combination with a phosphodiesterase inhibitor can produce profound, refractory hypotension that a routine allergy/med-history question would miss.
atScene.zh: 给任何胸痛病人硝酸甘油之前，一定要专门问一句过去 24-48 小时有没有吃过治疗勃起功能障碍的药——和磷酸二酯酶抑制剂合用可能造成难以纠正的严重低血压，而这一点常规的过敏/用药史问诊很容易漏问。

confusions.en: 'The PCP written exam and the BC practical exam test the same way' — false: the written paper is classification-only (12 buckets, zero drug names), while the practical station and licensing exam use real BC drug names and real BC doses. Study both layers separately.
confusions.zh: 「PCP 笔试和 BC 实操考考法一样」——错：笔试只考分类（12 个抽屉，零具名药），实操站和执照考用的却是真实 BC 药名和真实 BC 剂量。两层要分开准备。

confusions.en: 'No named drugs on the PCP written exam means I don't need to know real drug names' — false: you still have to know which BC medication fills each of the 12 classifications, because that mapping IS what most classification questions are testing indirectly, and because the practical/licensing exams demand the names outright.
confusions.zh: 「PCP 笔试不考具名药，所以我不用背真实药名」——错：你仍然要知道每个 BC 药具体对应 12 个分类里的哪一个，因为大多数分类题本质上就在间接考这个对应关系，而实操/执照考更是直接要你说出药名。

confusions.en: 'Ibuprofen and aspirin are interchangeable because both are NSAID-family' — false: aspirin's COX-1 selectivity gives it a specific antiplatelet effect that ibuprofen's COX-2-leaning selectivity does not reliably reproduce, which is exactly why aspirin — not ibuprofen — is the drug given for suspected ACS.
confusions.zh: 「布洛芬和阿司匹林可以互换，反正都是 NSAID」——错：阿司匹林靠 COX-1 选择性带来特有的抗血小板效果，布洛芬偏向 COX-2 的选择性并不能可靠地重现这个效果，这正是疑似 ACS 时用阿司匹林而不是布洛芬的原因。

confusions.en: 'A beta-blocked patient in hypovolemic shock will show the same warning signs as anyone else' — false: the classic early tachycardia of compensated shock can be blunted or absent because the beta blocker prevents the reflex heart-rate rise, so the first obvious sign may come later and hit harder.
confusions.zh: 「用着 β 受体阻滞剂的低血容量休克病人，警示信号和别人一样」——错：休克代偿期典型的早期心动过速可能被削弱甚至完全消失，因为 β 阻滞剂挡住了反射性心率上升，第一个明显信号可能来得更晚、也更凶。

confusions.en: 'The ET (tracheal) route is a reliable IV substitute in cardiac arrest' — false: absorption via the tracheal route is unreliable enough that it is no longer recommended in cardiac arrest at all; IV and IO are preferred, and even when ET is used elsewhere, the dose must be doubled.
confusions.zh: 「心脏骤停时气管（ET）途径可以可靠地替代 IV」——错：气管途径的吸收太不可靠，心脏骤停时已经完全不推荐使用；首选 IV 和 IO，即使在其他场景用 ET，剂量也必须翻倍。

mnemonics.name: ALIEN
mnemonics.en: The four medications suitable for the tracheal (ET) route: Atropine, Lidocaine, Epinephrine, Naloxone — remember the dose must be doubled versus IV.
mnemonics.zh: 适合气管（ET）给药的四个药——ALIEN：阿托品（Atropine）、利多卡因（Lidocaine）、肾上腺素（Epinephrine）、纳洛酮（Naloxone）——记得剂量要比 IV 翻倍。

mnemonics.name: SLUDGEM
mnemonics.en: Excess cholinergic (parasympathetic) stimulation: Salivation, Lacrimation, Urination, Defecation, GI upset, Emesis, Miosis — the toxidrome of organophosphates and nerve agents.
mnemonics.zh: 胆碱能（副交感）过度刺激的表现——SLUDGEM：流涎、流泪、排尿、排便、胃肠不适、呕吐、瞳孔缩小——有机磷和神经毒剂中毒的经典综合征。

mnemonics.name: 1-2-2-2-2 分类记数
mnemonics.en: Only two PCP classifications double up on named drugs — Antiemetic (dimenhydrinate + ondansetron) and Carbohydrate (D10W + oral glucose) — the other 10 are strict one-to-one pairs.
mnemonics.zh: 12 个 PCP 分类里只有两个对应两款药——止吐药（茶苯海明＋昂丹司琼）和碳水化合物（D10W＋口服葡萄糖）——其余 10 个都是严格的一对一配对。

selfCheck.qEn: A PCP written-exam question describes 'a vasodilator given sublingually for chest pain.' Which named BC drug is it testing, and why would the question never say the drug's actual name?
selfCheck.qZh: PCP 笔试题描述「一种舌下给药、用于治疗胸痛的血管扩张药」。这在考哪个 BC 具名药？题目为什么绝不会直接写出药名？
selfCheck.aEn: Nitroglycerin. Per COPR's 2026 exam-content rules, the PCP written paper tests only the 12 classifications and never names a specific drug — it will always describe the classification (vasodilator) and clinical context instead, leaving you to supply the name-level knowledge (nitroglycerin, SL, 0.4 mg q3-5min if SBP stays over 110) yourself.
selfCheck.aZh: 硝酸甘油。根据 COPR 2026 年的考纲规则，PCP 笔试只考 12 个分类、绝不点名具体药物——题目永远只会描述分类（血管扩张药）和临床场景，具名层面的知识（硝酸甘油、舌下、0.4 mg 每 3-5 分钟一次、前提是收缩压维持 >110）要你自己补上。

selfCheck.qEn: Name the four adrenergic receptor types and, for each, state the one-line clinical effect of stimulating it.
selfCheck.qZh: 说出四种肾上腺素能受体类型，并各说一句「激动它会产生什么临床效应」。
selfCheck.aEn: Alpha-1: peripheral vasoconstriction (raises BP). Alpha-2: controls norepinephrine release. Beta-1: raises heart rate, contractility, automaticity, conduction (used in cardiac arrest/hypotension). Beta-2: vasodilation and bronchodilation (used in asthma).
selfCheck.aZh: α1：外周血管收缩（升血压）。α2：控制去甲肾上腺素的释放。β1：提高心率、收缩力、自律性、传导（用于心脏骤停/低血压）。β2：血管扩张和支气管扩张（用于哮喘）。

selfCheck.qEn: A trauma patient takes warfarin. A different patient takes aspirin. Explain, in one sentence each, why you need to know this before you finish your primary survey.
selfCheck.qZh: 一名创伤病人在服用华法林，另一名在服用阿司匹林。请各用一句话说明，为什么你在完成初步评估之前就要知道这件事。
selfCheck.aEn: Warfarin blocks synthesis of vitamin-K-dependent clotting factors, so even a seemingly minor injury can bleed catastrophically and a minor head injury can turn lethal with delay. Aspirin inhibits platelet aggregation via COX-1, so it similarly raises bleeding risk from any traumatic injury, though through a different mechanism (platelets, not clotting factors).
selfCheck.aZh: 华法林阻断维生素 K 依赖性凝血因子的合成，所以即使看起来很轻的伤也可能大出血，轻微头外伤拖延处理也可能致命。阿司匹林经 COX-1 抑制血小板聚集，同样会提高任何外伤的出血风险，只是机制不同（作用在血小板，不是凝血因子）。

selfCheck.qEn: Using the reusable formulas from this chapter, calculate the IV drip rate (gtt/min) for a 250 mL bag to be infused over 20 minutes with a 15 gtts/mL set.
selfCheck.qZh: 用本章的通用公式，计算 250 mL 药袋、用 15 gtts/mL 输液器、要在 20 分钟内输完时的滴速（gtt/min）。
selfCheck.aEn: gtt/min = (volume x drop factor) / time = (250 mL x 15 gtts/mL) / 20 min = 3,750 / 20 = 187.5, so about 188 gtt/min (roughly 3 drops per second).
selfCheck.aZh: gtt/min＝（体积×点滴系数）÷时间＝（250 mL×15 gtts/mL）÷20 min＝3,750÷20＝187.5，约 188 gtt/min（大约每秒 3 滴）。

selfCheck.qEn: Which four of BC's 18 named drugs carry no COPR PCP classification, and what does that mean for how you should study them?
selfCheck.qZh: BC 18 份药物专论里哪 4 款没有 COPR PCP 分类？这对你怎么复习它们有什么影响？
selfCheck.aEn: Dexamethasone, Entonox (nitrous oxide), methoxyflurane (Penthrox), and TXA. It means the PCP written paper will never test them even indirectly by classification — but they are still fully examinable on the BC EMALB practical station and licensing exam, so they need to be studied as pure named-drug monographs (dose, route, onset, contraindications), not folded into any classification-recognition drill.
selfCheck.aZh: 地塞米松、Entonox（一氧化二氮/笑气）、甲氧氟烷（Penthrox）和 TXA。这意味着 PCP 笔试哪怕间接也不会通过分类考到它们——但它们在 BC EMALB 实操站和执照考里仍然是完全可考的，所以要按纯具名药专论（剂量、途径、起效、禁忌）来复习，而不能套进任何「分类识别」的刷题套路里。

bcAlerts.topicEn: Named drugs and classifications: exam scope by licence level
bcAlerts.topicZh: 具名药与分类：按执照等级划分的考试范围
bcAlerts.bookEn: Chapter 7's own classification tables (Section: Medication Classifications) name over 60 drug categories and cite specific generic and trade-name drugs throughout — e.g. amiodarone/Cordarone, salbutamol, epinephrine — with no distinction drawn between what is 'testable' at different licence levels; the textbook simply teaches pharmacology as a unified subject.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 本章自己的分类表格（药物分类小节）点名了 60 多个药物分类，并且全程引用具体的通用名和商品名药物——例如胺碘酮/Cordarone、沙丁胺醇、肾上腺素——完全没有区分不同执照等级「能不能考」；教材只是把药理学当成一个统一的学科来讲。
bcAlerts.bcEn: COPR's official exam-content rules cut this very differently by licence level: the EMR written exam excludes ALL named medications and ALL drug classifications; the PCP written exam tests ONLY the 12 listed classifications and never names a drug; the BC EMALB practical stations and the licensing exam use real drug names and BC-specific doses (the 18 monographs in this site's drugs.json). Prepare classification-recognition for the PCP written paper and full named-drug monographs separately for the practical/licensing exams.
bcAlerts.bcZh: COPR 官方考纲对此的切法完全不同、并且按执照等级区分：EMR 笔试排除所有具名药物和所有药物分类；PCP 笔试只考清单里的 12 个分类，绝不点名具体药物；BC EMALB 实操站和执照考则使用真实药名和 BC 特定剂量（对应本站 drugs.json 里的 18 份专论）。备考时要把「PCP 笔试的分类识别」和「实操/执照考的具名药专论」分开准备，两套都不能少。
bcAlerts.ref: COPR List of Named Medications & Drug Classifications, V1.2 Feb 27 2026

bcAlerts.topicZh: 硝酸甘油给药的血压门槛
bcAlerts.bookEn: This chapter's own worked example patient list simply notes 'nitroglycerin as required for chest pain' with no numeric blood-pressure cut-off attached, and the general Table 7-4 absorption table gives sublingual onset only as a broad 3-5 minute range with no drug-specific figure.
bcAlerts.bookZh: 本章自己举例的病人用药清单只写「按需使用硝酸甘油治疗胸痛」，没有附带任何具体的血压切点；而通用的 Table 7-4 吸收速率表也只给出舌下给药「3-5 分钟」这样的宽泛区间，没有针对具体药物的数字。
bcAlerts.bcEn: BC's actual nitroglycerin monograph is far more specific and IS what gets tested: 0.4 mg SL, repeatable every 3-5 minutes until pain-free, but ONLY while systolic BP stays above 110 mm Hg — and its measured onset is a sharp 60 seconds, not the book's generic 3-5 minute sublingual range. Always answer with the drug-specific BC number, not the textbook's general-route table.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 硝酸甘油的实际专论具体得多，而且这才是要考的内容：舌下 0.4 mg，每 3-5 分钟可重复一次直到无痛，但前提是收缩压必须一直维持在 110 mm Hg 以上——而且它实测的起效时间是明确的 60 秒，不是教材舌下给药那个笼统的 3-5 分钟区间。答题时要用药物专属的 BC 数字，不要套教材的通用途径表。
bcAlerts.ref: BC drugs.json nitroglycerin monograph; BC Provincial Exam Guidelines p.58-78

bcAlerts.topicEn: Table 7-4's general onset ranges vs. drug-specific BC monograph numbers
bcAlerts.topicZh: Table 7-4 的通用起效区间 vs BC 专论的具体数字
bcAlerts.bookEn: Table 7-4 gives one onset range per ROUTE, averaged across all drugs given that way — e.g. 'IM injection: 10-20 min' and 'IV: 30-60 s' — treating every drug given by a route as behaving identically.
bcAlerts.bookZh: Table 7-4 是按「途径」给出一个通用起效区间，把走这条途径的所有药都算作差不多——例如「肌肉注射：10-20 分钟」「静脉：30-60 秒」，相当于假设同一途径下所有药表现一致。
bcAlerts.bcEn: Individual BC monographs frequently diverge from that generic table — glucagon (IM) has a specific 15-minute onset and 15-minute peak with a 90-minute duration; naloxone's onset is drug-specific per route (IV 1 min, IM 3 min, IN 3 min) rather than a single blended range; epinephrine IM for anaphylaxis is specifically 5-15 minutes. When a written or practical question asks about a SPECIFIC named drug, answer with that drug's own monograph number from drugs.json, not Table 7-4's route-average.
bcAlerts.bcZh: BC 各药专论经常和这张通用表对不上——胰高血糖素（肌注）有自己明确的数字：15 分钟起效、15 分钟达峰、持续 90 分钟；纳洛酮的起效按途径各不相同（IV 1 分钟、IM 3 分钟、IN 3 分钟），而不是一个笼统的合并区间；肾上腺素肌注治疗过敏反应具体是 5-15 分钟。笔试或实操问到某个具体药物时，要答 drugs.json 里那款药自己专论的数字，不要套 Table 7-4 的「按途径平均」。
bcAlerts.ref: BC drugs.json glucagon/naloxone/epinephrine monographs vs. Nancy Table 7-4
